# SEO & Sharing Metadata Checklist: Site foundation for doncoleman.ca

**Purpose**: Validate that the spec's and plan's requirements for search-engine discoverability and social sharing are complete, unambiguous, consistent and measurable — covering per-deployment canonicals, noindex on every deployment, Open Graph/Twitter card metadata, the sitemap, and the 404 status for the not-found page.
**Created**: 2026-09-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) / [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements. It tests the requirements themselves, not the implementation.

## Canonical Address Requirements (Per Served Origin)

- [x] CHK001 Is "the address of the deployment the page is served from, determined at build time" specified precisely enough to know exactly which signal (env var, header, build context) determines it, or is the mechanism left entirely to the plan without a spec-level constraint on reliability? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK002 Is the fallback rule ("https://doncoleman.ca... when the build cannot determine it") given an explicit trigger condition — what counts as "cannot determine" — so it's testable rather than judgement-based? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK003 Are canonical-address requirements stated consistently across FR-017 (page metadata), FR-018 (sitemap), and FR-019 (noindex), so all three are guaranteed to agree on the same origin for a given deployment? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, FR-018, FR-019]
- [x] CHK004 Does the spec define what "a preview points to itself" means when a branch is rebuilt or redeployed with a new preview alias — is address stability across redeploys of the same branch specified? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §US4 Acceptance Scenario 5]
- [x] CHK005 Is the trailing-slash / URL-normalization convention for canonical and sitemap addresses specified anywhere, to avoid inconsistent forms between canonical tags and sitemap entries? [Gap, Spec §FR-017, FR-018]

## Noindex-on-Every-Deployment Requirements

- [x] CHK006 Is "every deployment... on every path" (FR-019) explicit about which mechanism(s) qualify (meta robots tag, X-Robots-Tag header, robots.txt disallow) or does it leave open whether one, some, or all are required, risking inconsistent implementation? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK007 Is it specified how the noindex requirement composes with the sitemap requirement (FR-018) — i.e., does a noindexed deployment still publish a sitemap, and is that combination intentional or contradictory? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018 vs. FR-019]
- [x] CHK008 Is the removal condition for the noindex instruction ("until the domain switch") tied to a concrete, verifiable trigger (e.g., a config flag) rather than an informal milestone, so a future feature can test for it? [Measurability, Spec §FR-019, Out of Scope §Domain switch]
- [x] CHK009 Does the spec address whether the main build's own noindex status must be independently testable from branch-preview noindex status (two acceptance paths), or is one test assumed to cover both? [Coverage, Spec §US4 Acceptance Scenario 4]

## Open Graph / Twitter Card Requirements

- [x] CHK010 Are the required Open Graph/Twitter fields enumerated exhaustively (title, description, canonical, image, alt text, page type, site name) with none left as "etc.", so completeness is verifiable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK011 Is the sharing-image requirement specified with concrete constraints (dimensions, format) anywhere in the spec, or only inferred from the plan's `og-default.png` (1200×630)? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-017 vs. Plan §Project Structure]
- [x] CHK012 Is the site-wide default behaviour (FR-017 / US4 Acceptance Scenario 2) specified per-field — i.e., can a page override only the image while inheriting the default description, or must overrides be all-or-nothing? [Ambiguity, Spec §US4 Acceptance Scenario 2]
- [x] CHK013 Is "page type" given an enumerated set of allowed values (e.g., website, article) relevant to this feature's pages (placeholder home, not-found), so the requirement is unambiguous for a reader without OG expertise? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK014 Does the spec require the not-found page to carry sharing metadata (or explicitly exempt it), given FR-017 says "every public page" and the not-found page is excluded from the sitemap (FR-018) but not clearly excluded from "public page" for metadata purposes? [Consistency, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017, FR-018, FR-016]

## Sitemap Requirements

- [x] CHK015 Is "every public page" for the sitemap defined with a concrete inclusion rule (e.g., all prerendered pages except 404) so it's unambiguous which of the two pages in this feature's scope (placeholder home) are included? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK016 Is the sitemap's reference "from its crawler instructions" (robots.txt) specified as to format/location precisely enough to be objectively checkable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK017 Is there a requirement for sitemap freshness/regeneration triggers (e.g., every build) so staleness across deployments isn't left ambiguous? [Gap]

## 404 Status & Not-Found Page Requirements

- [x] CHK018 Is the exact HTTP status code required for not-found requests stated numerically (404) rather than only as "a not-found status," to remove any implementation ambiguity? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016, US5 Acceptance Scenario 1]
- [x] CHK019 Is it specified that the 404 status must be returned for genuinely nonexistent addresses (including the enumerated old blog paths) and not accidentally for pages that exist but are still placeholders (FR-006's "future destinations")? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006 vs. FR-016, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK020 Are the acceptance criteria for verifying the 404 status testable independently of the page's visual content (i.e., is status-code verification separated from content verification in the requirements)? [Measurability, Spec §US5 Acceptance Scenario 1]
- [x] CHK021 Is the interaction between static hosting's not-found handling (a build-time generated 404 page served for any unmatched path) and true request-time status-code delivery addressed as a requirement, given Static-by-Default (Principle V) forbids per-request rendering? [Consistency, Spec §FR-023 vs. FR-016, Plan §Constitution Check Principle V]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK022 Is SC-006 ("zero public pages... missing either" sitemap entry or sharing metadata) measurable given the feature currently ships only a placeholder home page — does the spec define what "public page" count applies to this slice specifically? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK023 Is there a defined, repeatable method referenced for "run a built page through a sharing-preview inspector" (US4 Independent Test), or is the verification method left informal? [Gap, Spec §US4]
